objects.definition:
typedef struct
{
  int NewFile;                          /* is in new file mode? */
  int verbose;                          /* 0 = quiet, 1 = normal, 2 = verbose */
  int KeepDate;                         /* should keep date stamp? */
  int ConvMode;                         /* 0: ascii, 1: 7bit, 2: iso */
  int FromToMode;                       /* 0: dos2unix/unix2dos, 1: mac2unix/unix2mac */
  int NewLine;                          /* if TRUE, then additional newline */
  int Force;                            /* if TRUE, force conversion of all files. */
  int AllowChown;                       /* if TRUE, allow file ownership change in old file mode. */
  int Follow;                           /* 0: skip symlink, 1: follow symbolic link, 2: replace symlink. */
  int status;
  int stdio_mode;                       /* if TRUE, stdio mode */
  int to_stdout;                        /* write output to stdout in old file mode */
  int error;                            /* an error occurred */
  int bomtype;                          /* byte order mark */
  int add_bom;                          /* 1: write BOM */
  int keep_bom;                         /* 1: write BOM if input file has BOM. 0: Do not write BOM */
  int keep_utf16;                       /* 1: write UTF-16 format when input file is UTF-16 format */
  int file_info;                        /* 1: print file information */
  int locale_target;                    /* locale conversion target. 0: UTF-8; 1: GB18030 */
  unsigned int line_nr;                 /* line number where UTF-16 error occurs */
  int add_eol;                          /* Add End Of Line to last line */
} CFlag;
objects.description: Configuration and state flags for conversion operations (dos2unix/unix2dos/mac conversions). Holds mode selections, BOM handling, error/status flags, I/O choices, and locale/encoding options. Use an instance per conversion run; fields are read and updated by many API functions in this library.

functions.name: symbolic_link
functions.description: Returns whether the given path refers to a symbolic link. Intended for deciding how to treat files that may be symlinks on platforms that support them.
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated string
On platforms without symlink support, behavior may be platform-adapted (implementation-defined)

functions.name: regfile
functions.signature: int regfile(char *path, int allowSymlinks, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname);
functions.description: Checks whether the path refers to a regular file, optionally allowing symlinks, and may update flags/status in ipFlag. Typically used before performing file conversions.
requirements: path must be a valid, writable, null-terminated string (may be modified in-place)
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string identifying the program
allowSymlinks should be 0 or 1 indicating if symlinks are acceptable

functions.name: regfile_target
functions.description: Checks whether the target of the given path is a regular file, likely used for output/target files. May update flags/status in ipFlag.
requirements: path must be a valid, writable, null-terminated string (may be modified)
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string

functions.name: PrintUsage
functions.description: Prints command-line usage information for the program.
requirements: progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: PrintBSDLicense
functions.description: Prints the program’s BSD-style license text to standard output.
requirements: May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: PrintVersion
functions.description: Prints version information, possibly including localization details. localedir may indicate where locale files reside.
requirements: progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
localedir must be a valid, null-terminated string (may be unused depending on build)
May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: PrintLocaledir
functions.description: Prints or reports the active locale directory. Only available when ENABLE_NLS is defined at build time.
requirements: This function is available only if ENABLE_NLS is defined
localedir must be a valid, null-terminated string
May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: OpenInFile
functions.description: Opens the specified file for reading in the appropriate mode for the platform and returns a FILE pointer.
requirements: ipFN must be a valid, null-terminated path string
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle errors
On systems requiring binary mode for data, the function will select the correct mode internally

functions.name: OpenOutFile
functions.description: Opens the specified file for writing (creating/truncating as needed) and returns a FILE pointer.
requirements: opFN must be a valid, null-terminated path string
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle errors
File will be opened in a platform-appropriate mode (binary vs text as configured)

functions.name: OpenOutFiled
functions.description: Wraps an existing file descriptor as a FILE* for writing (likely via fdopen).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor with suitable write permissions
Caller must check the returned FILE* for NULL and handle errors
Ownership/lifetime: closing the returned FILE* will typically close fd

functions.name: dirname
functions.description: Returns the directory component of a path, possibly modifying the input buffer and returning a pointer to it. This fallback declaration is present for certain platforms (e.g., Turbo C or MSYS).
requirements: Available only when compiled on platforms where this header provides dirname (e.g., __TURBOC__ or __MSYS__)
path must be a writable, null-terminated string; contents may be modified
Returned pointer may point inside path; caller must not free it

functions.name: MakeTempFileFrom
functions.description: Creates and opens a temporary file related to OutFN and returns both the FILE* and the generated temporary filename via fname_ret.
requirements: OutFN must be a valid, null-terminated string (used as a basis for temp naming)
fname_ret must be a non-null pointer to char*; on success, *fname_ret will be set to a newly allocated null-terminated filename that the caller must free
Caller must check the FILE* return for NULL and handle errors

functions.name: ResolveSymbolicLink
functions.signature: int ResolveSymbolicLink(char *lFN, char **rFN, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname);
functions.description: Resolves a pathname that may be a symbolic link. On success, returns information and provides the resolved path via rFN.
requirements: lFN must be a valid, writable, null-terminated string
rFN must be a non-null pointer to char*; on success, *rFN is set to a newly allocated resolved path that the caller must free
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Behavior may vary on platforms without symlink support

functions.name: read_bom
functions.description: Examines the start of the stream for a Unicode Byte Order Mark (BOM) and sets bomtype accordingly. Returns a FILE* usable for subsequent reading (typically the same as f).
requirements: f must be a valid, open FILE* positioned at the start of the stream to detect a BOM correctly
bomtype must be a non-null pointer; on success, *bomtype is set to one of the BOM type constants defined in this header
Caller must handle a NULL return to indicate an error

functions.name: write_bom
functions.description: Writes a Unicode BOM to the output stream if requested by flags (e.g., add_bom/keep_bom/keep_utf16). Returns a FILE* for continued writing.
requirements: f must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag whose BOM-related fields control behavior
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string used for messages/errors
Caller must check for NULL return to detect errors

functions.name: print_bom
functions.signature: void print_bom (const int bomtype, const char *filename, const char *progname);
functions.description: Prints information about the detected BOM type for the given filename, typically for verbose or info output.
requirements: filename and progname must be valid, null-terminated strings
bomtype must be one of the defined BOM constants

functions.name: check_unicode
functions.signature: int check_unicode(FILE *InF, FILE *TempF,  CFlag *ipFlag, const char *ipInFN, const char *progname);
functions.description: Checks the input file for Unicode encoding properties and writes any necessary transformed content to a temporary file. Updates CFlag with status such as errors or BOM details.
requirements: InF must be a valid, open FILE* for reading
TempF must be a valid, open FILE* for writing temporary data
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag (fields like bomtype, error, line_nr may be updated)
ipInFN and progname must be valid, null-terminated strings
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success/failure

functions.name: print_messages_stdio
functions.description: Prints summary/status messages for stdio mode conversions based on flags in pFlag.
requirements: pFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: print_messages_newfile
functions.signature: void print_messages_newfile(const CFlag *pFlag, const char *infile, const char *outfile, const char *progname, const int RetVal);
functions.description: Prints summary/status messages for conversions that produce a new output file, using RetVal and flags to determine what to report.
requirements: pFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
infile, outfile, and progname must be valid, null-terminated strings
RetVal must be the result code from the conversion routine
May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: print_messages_oldfile
functions.signature: void print_messages_oldfile(const CFlag *pFlag, const char *infile, const char *progname, const int RetVal);
functions.description: Prints summary/status messages for in-place (old file) conversions, using RetVal and flags to determine output.
requirements: pFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
infile and progname must be valid, null-terminated strings
RetVal must be the result code from the conversion routine
May write to stdout or stderr

functions.name: ConvertNewFile
functions.signature: int ConvertNewFile(char *ipInFN, char *ipOutFN, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname, int (*Convert)(FILE*, FILE*, CFlag *, const char *));
functions.description: High-level helper that converts an input file to a new output file using the provided Convert callback for byte/mbs processing. Manages opening, BOM handling, and messaging according to flags.
requirements: ipInFN and ipOutFN must be valid, null-terminated path strings
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Convert must be a non-null function pointer implementing the conversion: it must read from FILE* in, write to FILE* out, honor ipFlag, and return an int status
Caller must check the returned int for success/failure

functions.name: ConvertStdio
functions.signature: int ConvertStdio(CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname, int (*Convert)(FILE*, FILE*, CFlag *, const char *));
functions.description: Performs conversion in stdio mode (stdin to stdout) using the provided Convert callback for byte/mbs processing.
requirements: ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Convert must be a non-null function pointer implementing conversion semantics compatible with stdio streams
Caller must check the returned int for success/failure

functions.name: parse_options
functions.signature: int parse_options(int argc, char *argv[], CFlag *pFlag, const char *localedir, const char *progname, void (*PrintLicense)(void), int (*Convert)(FILE*, FILE*, CFlag *, const char *));
functions.description: Parses command-line options, initializes pFlag, and selects/uses the provided conversion and licensing callbacks. Returns a status code indicating how to proceed.
requirements: argv must be an array of argc C strings; each element must be a valid, null-terminated string
pFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag (fields will be updated)
localedir and progname must be valid, null-terminated strings
PrintLicense must be a non-null function pointer to a void(void) function
Convert must be a non-null conversion function pointer
Caller must check the integer return value to determine next steps (e.g., success, help/version printed, errors)

functions.name: d2u_getc_error
functions.description: Handles/report errors related to character input (getc) operations, updating flags and printing messages as needed.
requirements: ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
May set ipFlag->error and write to stderr

functions.name: d2u_putc_error
functions.description: Handles/reports errors related to character output (putc) operations, updating flags and printing messages as needed.
requirements: ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
May set ipFlag->error and write to stderr

functions.name: d2u_putwc_error
functions.description: Handles/reports errors related to wide-character output (putwc) operations. Available only when D2U_UNICODE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNICODE is defined at build time
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string

functions.name: d2u_getwc
functions.description: Reads a wide character from the stream according to the detected BOM/encoding. Available only when D2U_UNICODE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNICODE is defined at build time
f must be a valid, open FILE* for reading
bomtype must be set to a supported BOM/encoding indicator (e.g., FILE_UTF16LE/BE, UTF-8)
Caller must check for WEOF to detect errors/EOF

functions.name: d2u_ungetwc
functions.signature: wint_t d2u_ungetwc(wint_t wc, FILE *f, int bomtype);
functions.description: Pushes a wide character back onto the input stream consistent with the current encoding. Available only when D2U_UNICODE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNICODE is defined at build time
f must be a valid, open FILE*
wc must be a valid wide character or WEOF as appropriate
bomtype must match the encoding used for reading

functions.name: d2u_putwc
functions.signature: wint_t d2u_putwc(wint_t wc, FILE *f, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname);
functions.description: Writes a wide character to the output stream in the encoding dictated by ipFlag/BOM settings. Available only when D2U_UNICODE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNICODE is defined at build time
f must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag with encoding/BOM preferences
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Caller must check the return value; WEOF indicates failure

functions.name: d2u_strncpy
functions.description: Safe string copy utility that copies src into dest, bounded by dest_size, ensuring proper termination semantics per the implementation.
requirements: dest must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of size at least dest_size
src must be a valid, null-terminated string
dest_size must be the actual capacity of dest in bytes
Caller should ensure dest_size > 0 and check the resulting contents for truncation as needed

functions.name: d2u_utf8_fprintf
functions.signature: void d2u_utf8_fprintf( FILE *stream, const char* format, ... );
functions.description: fprintf-like function that writes UTF-8 encoded output to stream. Available when D2U_UNIFILE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNIFILE is defined at build time
stream must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
format must be a valid, null-terminated format string; variadic arguments must match the format

functions.name: d2u_ansi_fprintf
functions.signature: void d2u_ansi_fprintf( FILE *stream, const char* format, ... );
functions.description: fprintf-like function that writes ANSI (system code page) encoded output to stream. Available when D2U_UNIFILE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNIFILE is defined at build time
stream must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
format must be a valid, null-terminated format string; variadic arguments must match the format

functions.name: glob_warg
functions.signature: int glob_warg(int argc, wchar_t *wargv[], char ***argv, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname);
functions.description: Expands wide-character command-line arguments (e.g., Windows Unicode argv) into a UTF-8/ANSI argv array for downstream processing. Available when D2U_UNIFILE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNIFILE is defined at build time
wargv must be an array of argc wide strings; each element must be a valid, null-terminated wchar_t string
argv must be a non-null pointer to a char** array output; on success, *argv is set to an allocated array of C strings the caller must free (both array and its elements)
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Caller must check the int return value for success/failure

functions.name: ConvertDosToUnixW
functions.signature: int ConvertDosToUnixW(FILE* ipInF, FILE* ipOutF, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname);
functions.description: Performs DOS-to-UNIX line ending conversion in Unicode/wide mode, honoring flags (e.g., BOM handling). Available only when D2U_UNICODE is defined.
requirements: This function is available only if D2U_UNICODE is defined at build time
ipInF must be a valid, open FILE* for reading
ipOutF must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Caller must check the returned int for success/failure

functions.name: ConvertDosToUnix
functions.signature: int ConvertDosToUnix(FILE* ipInF, FILE* ipOutF, CFlag *ipFlag, const char *progname);
functions.description: Performs DOS-to-UNIX line ending conversion on byte/multibyte streams, honoring flags (e.g., BOM handling).
requirements: ipInF must be a valid, open FILE* for reading
ipOutF must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
ipFlag must be a non-null pointer to an initialized CFlag
progname must be a valid, null-terminated string
Caller must check the returned int for success/failure

data_types.description: A null-terminated string representing a file system path or filename. May be absolute or relative and can include directories, extensions, and platform-specific separators.
A null-terminated string used to identify the running program in messages. Typically argv[0]-like; any non-empty ASCII/UTF-8 string is acceptable.
Arbitrary bytes stored in a file, not constrained to text; may include BOMs, UTF-8/UTF-16 sequences, or any random byte values.
A null-terminated string intended to be displayed or logged as a file name. Similar to filesystem path; may be just a base name.
A null-terminated command-line argument string as would appear in argv[], including flags (e.g., -v), options, or file paths. No specific format required.
A generic null-terminated string buffer with no required format or character set; can be any bytes excluding the terminating NUL.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid filesystem path strings and related argv-like
# strings to exercise the target stubs. It focuses on:
# - Valid, null-terminated C strings (the harness adds terminator; we provide bytes)
# - Paths covering different platforms, separators, symlinky names, temp-like names
# - Program names, locale dirs, and general argument-style strings
# The fuzzer harness pulls buffers via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME from the same input.
# We therefore pack multiple NUL-terminated strings into one buffer so that the
# harness can slice them deterministically.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Utilities to build pools of interesting values
POSIX_DIRS = [b"/", b"/tmp", b"/var/tmp", b"/home/user", b"./", b"../", b"./sub", b"../sub"]
WIN_DRIVES = [b"C:", b"D:", b"E:"]
WIN_DIRS = [b"C:\\", b"C:\\Temp", b"C:\\Windows", b"C:\\Users\\Public", b".\\", b"..\\"]
BASENAMES = [
    b"file", b"data", b"input", b"output", b"symlink", b"link", b"config", b"readme",
    b"a", b"b", b"longfilename_with-dash.and.dot", b"unicodename",
]
EXTS = [b"", b".txt", b".bin", b".log", b".csv", b".dat", b".utf8", b".utf16", b".tmp"]

# Include names likely to exercise symlink/regular file checks
SPECIAL_NAMES = [
    b".hidden", b"..dotdot", b".gitignore", b"/dev/null", b"/proc/self/exe",
    b"CON", b"NUL", b"PRN", b"AUX", b"LPT1", b"COM1",
]

# Program names and locale directories
PROG_NAMES = [b"dos2unix", b"unix2dos", b"myprog", b"converter", b"tool", b"d2u"]
LOCALES = [b"/usr/share/locale", b"/usr/local/share/locale", b"C:\\Locale", b"./locale", b"/tmp/locale"]

# Content-like strings for data written into files and general FUZZ_PARAM_STR
DATA_SNIPPETS = [
    b"Hello World\n",
    b"Line1\r\nLine2\nLine3\r\n",
    b"UTF-8: caf\xC3\xA9, snowman \xE2\x98\x83\n",
    b"BOM-UTF8:\xEF\xBB\xBFStart\n",
    b"UTF-16LE BOM:\xff\xfeA\x00B\x00\n\x00",
    b"No newlines at EOF",
    b"\r\n\r\nLeading CRLF then text\n",
]

# Helper to generate a path with randomness and platform variety
def gen_path(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose platform style
    style = rng.choice(["posix", "win", "relative"])  # relative applies to both
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    if style == "posix":
        base = rng.choice(POSIX_DIRS)
        parts.append(base.rstrip(b"/"))
        # append 0-3 subdirs
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            name = rng.choice(BASENAMES + [b"dir", b"subdir", b"temp"]) + rng.choice([b"", b"-sub"])  \
                   + rng.choice([b"", b"_" + str(rng.randint(0, 999)).encode()])
            parts.append(name)
        # basename
        basefile = rng.choice(BASENAMES + SPECIAL_NAMES)
        ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
        path = b"/".join([p for p in parts if p])
        if path == b"":
            path = b"/"
        # avoid double slash unless root
        if path != b"/":
            path += b"/"
        return path + basefile + ext

    if style == "win":
        root = rng.choice(WIN_DIRS + WIN_DRIVES)
        sep = b"\\"
        path = root
        # 0-3 subdirs
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            sd = rng.choice([b"Temp", b"Data", b"Sub", b"Dir"]) + rng.choice([b"", b"_%d" % rng.randint(0, 999)])
            if not path.endswith(sep):
                path += sep
            path += sd
        if not path.endswith(sep):
            path += sep
        basefile = rng.choice(BASENAMES + SPECIAL_NAMES)
        ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
        return path + basefile + ext

    # relative
    prefix = rng.choice([b"./", b"../", b"", b".\\", b"..\\"])
    sep = b"/" if b"\\" not in prefix else b"\\"
    segs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        segs.append(rng.choice([b"sub", b"folder", b"tmp", b"build"]))
    basefile = rng.choice(BASENAMES)
    ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    mid = sep.join(segs)
    if mid:
        return prefix + mid + sep + basefile + ext
    else:
        return prefix + basefile + ext

# Helper to generate general non-empty strings (argv, program, etc.)
def gen_string(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if choice == 0:
        return rng.choice(PROG_NAMES)
    if choice == 1:
        return rng.choice(LOCALES)
    if choice == 2:
        return rng.choice(DATA_SNIPPETS)
    if choice == 3:
        # option-like
        opts = [b"-v", b"--verbose", b"-q", b"--keep-bom", b"--add-bom", b"-o", b"--newfile", b"--follow-symlinks"]
        val = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            val.append(rng.choice(opts))
        return b" ".join(val)
    if choice == 4:
        # random ascii word
        n = rng.randint(3, 16)
        return bytes([rng.choice(list(range(0x30, 0x7B))) for _ in range(n)])
    # fallback: path-like
    return gen_path(rng)

# Pack a sequence of strings as NUL-terminated slices
def pack_cstrs(items: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for it in items:
        # ensure no internal NULs to avoid premature termination
        it = it.split(b"\x00")[0]
        out += it + b"\x00"
        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

# We plan the order to satisfy the stubs which pull many FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME values
# Typical needs per run (upper bound):
# - Several filenames for file operations
# - Several general strings for progname/localedir/argv/content
# We'll interleave to offer variety regardless of consumption order.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create pools
    filenames: List[bytes] = []
    strings: List[bytes] = []

    # Generate a mix of filenames likely valid on host or at least parseable
    for _ in range(20):
        filenames.append(gen_path(rng))

    # Ensure some deterministic special cases
    filenames.extend([
        b"/tmp/fuzz_input.txt",
        b"/tmp/fuzz_output.txt",
        b"./relative.txt",
        b"C:\\Temp\\fuzz.txt",
        b"symlink_target",
    ])

    # General strings
    for _ in range(25):
        strings.append(gen_string(rng))

    # Ensure program names and locales present
    strings.extend([rng.choice(PROG_NAMES), rng.choice(LOCALES)])

    # Compose ordered items: interleave filenames and strings to satisfy varied consumption
    items: List[bytes] = []
    fi = si = 0
    while (fi < len(filenames) or si < len(strings)) and len(items) < 80:
        # Bias toward filenames since many stubs request filenames
        if fi < len(filenames):
            items.append(filenames[fi]); fi += 1
        if si < len(strings):
            items.append(strings[si]); si += 1
        # Occasionally add data snippet to be used as file content via FUZZ_PARAM_STR
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            items.append(rng.choice(DATA_SNIPPETS))

    buf = pack_cstrs(items)
    # Guarantee non-empty and within size
    if not buf:
        buf = b"x\x00"
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type targeted: "program name" strings that are valid, non-empty, null-terminated
# The fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME extensively. Our
# generator returns a single bytes buffer that the harness will slice to feed those
# calls in order. We therefore embed multiple sensible, valid C strings and paths
# in one buffer, separated by NUL (\0). Each consumer in the harness expects a
# valid, non-empty C string, so we construct a sequence of such strings to cover:
# - program names (argv[0]-like)
# - locale directory strings
# - general strings used as file names or display names
# - realistic filesystem paths including absolute, relative, dot components,
#   with and without symlink-like names, with different extensions
# - content payloads for file-based tests (e.g., Unicode BOMs + text)
# The fuzzer will read them in order via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PROGRAM_PREFIXES = [
    "dos2unix", "unix2dos", "d2u", "u2d", "converter", "tool", "app"
]

LOCALE_DIRS = [
    "/usr/share/locale", "/usr/local/share/locale", "/opt/locale",
    "./locale", "locale", "C:/locale", "C:/Program Files/App/locale"
]

# Some path components likely to trigger symlink/dirname/regular file logic
PATH_COMPONENTS = [
    "", ".", "..", "tmp", "var", "etc", "bin", "home", "symlinks",
    "links", "files", "data", "unicode", "spaces in name", "çøøl",
]

BASENAMES = [
    "input.txt", "output.txt", "Makefile", "README", "LICENSE",
    "data.bin", "test.dat", "file", "NUL.txt", "con.txt", "aux.txt",
    "résumé.txt", "emoji_😀.txt", "mac_eol.txt", "dos_eol.txt",
    "utf16le.txt", "utf16be.txt", "utf8.txt"
]

EXTS = ["", ".tmp", ".bak", ".out", ".new", ".lnk"]

# Useful payloads for BOM/Unicode checks and DOS/UNIX conversions
PAYLOADS = [
    b"Hello world\n",                          # LF only
    b"Line1\r\nLine2\r\n",                  # CRLF
    b"LineA\rLineB\r",                        # CR only (classic Mac)
    b"",                                        # empty
]

# UTF-8 with BOM
UTF8_BOM = b"\xEF\xBB\xBF"
# UTF-16LE BOM and some simple content (ASCII range -> valid when read as UTF-16LE)
UTF16LE_BOM = b"\xFF\xFE"
UTF16BE_BOM = b"\xFE\xFF"
# Minimal UTF-16 text for checks: "A\n" in LE/BE
UTF16LE_TEXT = UTF16LE_BOM + b"A\x00\n\x00"
UTF16BE_TEXT = UTF16BE_BOM + b"\x00A\x00\n"

# Some directory/path patterns to exercise absolute/relative and Windows/Unix
ABS_UNIX_DIRS = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/home/user", "/etc", "/"]
ABS_WIN_DIRS = ["C:/Temp", "C:/Windows", "C:/Users/Public", "D:/Data"]
REL_DIRS = [".", "..", "./tmp", "../data", "./build/out"]


def _rand(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(seq)


def _random_progname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand(rng, PROGRAM_PREFIXES)
    # Optionally append variant suffixes
    suffixes = ["", "-static", "-debug", "-test", "_v1", "_x64"]
    sfx = _rand(rng, suffixes)
    return base + sfx


def _random_localedir(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes absolute Unix, sometimes Windows, sometimes relative
    pick = rng.randint(0, 2)
    if pick == 0:
        return _rand(rng, LOCALE_DIRS)
    elif pick == 1:
        return _rand(rng, ABS_UNIX_DIRS)
    else:
        return _rand(rng, ABS_WIN_DIRS + REL_DIRS)


def _random_component(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    c = _rand(rng, PATH_COMPONENTS)
    # Sanitize to avoid embedded NUL
    return c.replace("\x00", "")


def _random_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    b = _rand(rng, BASENAMES)
    # Optionally vary case or add extension
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        b = b.upper()
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        b += _rand(rng, EXTS)
    return b


def _random_unix_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 2-4 components
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append("")  # leading slash for absolute
    n = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(n):
        comp = _random_component(rng)
        if comp:
            parts.append(comp)
    parts.append(_random_basename(rng))
    path = "/".join(parts)
    if path == "":
        path = "/tmp/file.txt"
    return path


def _random_win_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    drive = rng.choice(["C:", "D:", "E:"])
    comps = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(n):
        comp = _random_component(rng).replace("/", " ")
        comps.append(comp)
    comps.append(_random_basename(rng))
    return drive + "/" + "/".join(comps)


def _random_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pick = rng.random()
    if pick < 0.45:
        return _random_unix_path(rng)
    elif pick < 0.9:
        return _random_win_path(rng)
    else:
        # Relative
        return rng.choice(REL_DIRS) + "/" + _random_basename(rng)


def _random_display_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For print_bom filenames etc. Use short names with UTF-8 possibilities
    choices = [
        "file.txt", "input.dat", "résumé.txt", "emoji_😀.log", "a", "b", "temp",
        "symlink_target", "link", "路径.txt"
    ]
    return _rand(rng, choices)


def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .:/\\"
    s = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)).strip()
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    return s


def _build_payloads(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []
    # Program names used many times across stubs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        out.append(_random_progname(rng).encode("utf-8"))
    # Locale directories
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        out.append(_random_localedir(rng).encode("utf-8"))
    # Paths for regfile/regfile_target/ResolveSymbolicLink
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        out.append(_random_path(rng).encode("utf-8"))
    # Display/file names for print_bom and misc FUZZ_PARAM_STR users
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        out.append(_random_display_name(rng).encode("utf-8"))
    # Extra generic non-empty strings for argv in parse_options
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        out.append(_random_ascii(rng, 2, 8).encode("utf-8"))
    # Content strings for file writes (FUZZ_PARAM_STR feeding file content)
    content_choices = list(PAYLOADS)
    # Add BOM-ed payloads to exercise read_bom/check_unicode
    content_choices += [UTF8_BOM + b"UTF8 BOM text\n",
                        UTF16LE_TEXT,
                        UTF16BE_TEXT]
    # Add mixed line endings
    content_choices += [b"a\n\r\nb\r\nc\n", b"\r\n\r\nend\n"]
    rng.shuffle(content_choices)
    for c in content_choices[: rng.randint(3, 6) ]:
        out.append(c)
    return out


def _pack_cstrings_blobs(chunks: List[bytes], max_total: int) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated C strings in sequence; also include a few raw blobs
    # for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumers that write/read binary content.
    buf = bytearray()
    for part in chunks:
        if len(buf) + len(part) + 1 > max_total:
            break
        buf += part
        buf.append(0)  # NUL terminator
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts = _build_payloads(rng)
    data = _pack_cstrings_blobs(parts, MAX_TOTAL)
    # Ensure non-empty and under limit
    if not data:
        data = b"prog\x00/tmp/file.txt\x00locale\x00"
    return data

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for the print_bom fuzzer stub.
# The stub expects two FUZZ_PARAM_STR strings (filename and progname), both non-empty.
# The fuzzer provides an unsigned int separately for bomtype; we only need to supply the buffer
# that FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls from. Many fuzzers partition the provided buffer for multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in order; thus we will serialize two strings back-to-back with clear
# separators, offering a variety of valid yet interesting path/progname shapes.
#
# Format we emit (ASCII/UTF-8 friendly):
#   <fname>\n<progname>\n
MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-"

WIN_SEPS = ['\\\
']
POSIX_SEPS = ['/']

BASENAMES = [
    "file", "data", "input", "output", "README", "Makefile",
    "NUL", "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "COM1", "LPT1",
    "空间", "ファイル", "файл", "archivo", "فایل",
]

EXTS = ["", ".txt", ".bin", ".utf8", ".utf16", ".log", ".dat"]

PROGNAMES = [
    "dos2unix", "unix2dos", "mac2unix", "converter", "tool",
    "d2u", "u2d", "测试程序", "программа", "برنامج"
]

DRIVES = ["C:", "D:", "E:"]

UNICODE_SEGMENTS = [
    "Δ", "é", "ü", "ß", "ç", "ø", "å", "ñ", "字", "漢字", "🙂"
]

RESERVED_WIN = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL"} | {f"COM{i}" for i in range(1,10)} | {f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1,10)}


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]


def _rand_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_choice(rng, BASENAMES)
    # Randomly mix in unicode or safe chars
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        # append some unicode pieces
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
            base += _rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SEGMENTS)
    else:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            base += rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS)
    ext = _rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
    # Avoid creating reserved Windows names without an extension; add extension if needed
    if base.upper() in RESERVED_WIN and ext == "":
        ext = ".txt"
    return base + ext


def _rand_dirname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    style = rng.choice(["posix", "win"])  # choose path style
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        part = _rand_basename(rng)
        # sanitize separators inside a segment
        part = part.replace('/', '_').replace('\\', '_')
        parts.append(part)
    if style == "posix":
        root = "/" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
        return root + "/".join(parts) if parts else (root if root else "")
    else:
        # windows-style
        drive = _rand_choice(rng, DRIVES) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
        sep = "\\"
        prefix = drive + (sep if drive else (sep if rng.random() < 0.3 else ""))
        return prefix + sep.join(parts) if parts else (prefix if prefix else "")


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose directory + basename
    d = _rand_dirname(rng)
    b = _rand_basename(rng)
    if d:
        # choose separator consistent with style detected
        sep = "\\" if "\\" in d and not d.startswith("/") else "/"
        # Avoid double separators
        if d.endswith(sep):
            return d + b
        else:
            return d + sep + b
    return b


def _rand_progname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Program names are typically base names without path, but allow some with path
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return _rand_filename(rng)
    name = _rand_choice(rng, PROGNAMES)
    # optional suffix/prefix
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        name += str(rng.randint(0, 3))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        name += ".exe"
    return name


def _ensure_bounds(s: str) -> str:
    # Keep the entire payload <= MAX_TOTAL, leave room for newline between fields
    max_len = max(1, MAX_TOTAL - 2)  # at least two newlines, but we use one
    if len(s) > max_len:
        return s[:max_len]
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create filename and program strings; both must be non-empty
    fname = _rand_filename(rng)
    if not fname:
        fname = _rand_basename(rng)
    prog = _rand_progname(rng)
    if not prog:
        prog = "dos2unix"

    # Occasionally stress long names within valid limits
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # append additional segments while respecting size cap
        extra = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
            seg = _rand_basename(rng)
            seg = seg.replace('/', '_').replace('\\', '_')
            extra.append(seg)
        # Join with a separator matching current fname style
        sep = "\\" if ("\\" in fname and not fname.startswith("/")) else "/"
        candidate = fname + sep + sep.join(extra)
        if len(candidate) < MAX_TOTAL // 2:
            fname = candidate

    # Assemble buffer with newline separator; FUZZ harness will split by its own logic,
    # but providing two newline-terminated strings is a common and safe approach.
    payload = f"{_ensure_bounds(fname)}\n{_ensure_bounds(prog)}\n"

    # Ensure size bound
    if len(payload.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim conservatively from fname portion
        half = MAX_TOTAL // 2
        fname_trim = fname.encode('utf-8')[:half].decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        prog_trim = prog.encode('utf-8')[:(MAX_TOTAL - len(fname_trim) - 2)].decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        payload = f"{fname_trim}\n{prog_trim}\n"

    return payload.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets argv elements for parse_options of a dos2unix-like tool.
# Strategy:
# - Build a plausible argv array encoded as a single byte buffer with NUL-separated
#   C strings, as fuzzer harness pulls multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR values.
# - Include program name, locale dir, and 1-5 additional args covering flags,
#   options with/without arguments, encodings, verbosity, stdin/stdout modes,
#   BOM/Unicode toggles, and file paths.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Ensure all strings are non-empty and ASCII/UTF-8 safe.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Some representative flags and options commonly seen in dos2unix/unix2dos tools.
FLAGS_NOARG = [
    "-v", "-q", "--quiet", "--verbose",
    "-k", "--keepdate",
    "-f", "--force",
    "-n", "--newfile",
    "-o", "--oldfile",
    "--add-eol",
    "--allow-chown",
    "--follow-symlink", "--no-follow-symlink",
]

# Options that take a value following (either as next argv or joined with '=')
OPTIONS_WITH_VAL = [
    "--encoding", "--locale", "--output", "-o",
    "--input", "-i",
    "--bom", "--keep-bom", "--conv",
]

# Possible values for options
ENC_VALUES = ["utf-8", "UTF-8", "gb18030", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE"]
BOM_VALUES = ["add", "keep", "remove", "auto"]
CONV_VALUES = ["dos2unix", "unix2dos", "mac2unix", "unix2mac"]

# Some plausible locale directories and program names
PROG_NAMES = [
    "dos2unix", "unix2dos", "d2u", "u2d", "converter",
]
LOCALE_DIRS = [
    "/usr/share/locale", "/usr/local/share/locale", "./locale", "locale", "C:/locale",
]

# Sample file paths
FILE_NAMES = [
    "README.txt", "src/main.c", "data/input.txt", "C:/temp/in.txt", "out.bin",
    "./file with spaces.txt", "../relative/path.txt", "/tmp/in.out", "-",  # '-' for stdin/stdout
]

# Random helper

def _rand_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a mix of absolute/relative, with/without spaces and extensions.
    choices = FILE_NAMES + [
        f"/tmp/{r.choice(['a','b','test','data'])}{r.randint(0,999)}.txt",
        f"./{r.choice(['α','β','Γ']).encode('utf-8','ignore').decode('utf-8')}file{r.randint(0,9)}.log".replace("\\x", ""),
        f"C:/Users/user/Documents/file{r.randint(1,999)}.txt",
    ]
    return r.choice(choices)


def _rand_progname(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(PROG_NAMES)
    # occasionally add suffix/prefix
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        base += str(r.randint(1,3))
    return base


def _rand_localedir(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return r.choice(LOCALE_DIRS)
    # Constructed path
    segs = [r.choice(["/usr", "/opt", "/custom"]) , "share", "locale"]
    return "/".join(s.strip("/") for s in segs)


def _emit_arg_list(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    argv: List[str] = []
    # argv[0]
    argv.append(_rand_progname(r))

    # 1..N additional args (1..5)
    n = r.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(n):
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.45:
            argv.append(r.choice(FLAGS_NOARG))
        elif t < 0.8:
            opt = r.choice(OPTIONS_WITH_VAL)
            if opt in ("--encoding",):
                val = r.choice(ENC_VALUES)
            elif opt in ("--bom", "--keep-bom"):
                val = r.choice(BOM_VALUES)
            elif opt in ("--conv",):
                val = r.choice(CONV_VALUES)
            elif opt in ("--locale",):
                val = _rand_localedir(r)
            elif opt in ("--output", "-o"):
                val = _rand_path(r)
            elif opt in ("--input", "-i"):
                val = _rand_path(r)
            else:
                val = str(r.randint(0, 3))
            if r.random() < 0.5 and not opt.startswith("-"):
                # Fallback: just append value
                argv.append(opt)
                argv.append(val)
            else:
                # Use --opt=val form when long
                if opt.startswith("--") and r.random() < 0.8:
                    argv.append(f"{opt}={val}")
                else:
                    argv.append(opt)
                    argv.append(val)
        else:
            # Positional file arguments
            argv.append(_rand_path(r))

    return argv


def _build_buffer(argv: List[str], prog: str, loc: str) -> bytes:
    # Fuzzer stub asks FUZZ_PARAM_STR() twice first (prog, loc), then builds argv.
    # We concatenate: prog\0loc\0arg0\0arg1\0... to feed sequential pulls.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Ensure non-empty prog/loc
    if not prog:
        prog = "prog"
    if not loc:
        loc = "/usr/share/locale"
    parts.append(prog.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00")
    parts.append(loc.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00")
    for a in argv:
        s = a if a else "-v"
        parts.append(s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00")
    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # ensure last byte is NUL to terminate string safely
        if buf[-1] != 0:
            buf = buf[:-1] + b"\x00"
    return buf


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    prog = _rand_progname(r)
    loc = _rand_localedir(r)
    argv = _emit_arg_list(r)
    return _build_buffer(argv, prog, loc)
